name: Tacrolimus
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Oral and IV tacrolimus: tacrolimus is a calcineurin inhibitor metabolized by CYP3A in the liver and gut; under 1% is excreted unchanged in urine, and its pharmacokinetics are similar in kidney impairment and dialysis. The kidney issue is nephrotoxicity (acute and chronic) and hyperkalemia, so dosing follows whole-blood trough levels, at the lower end of the range when kidney function is already impaired. It is not dialyzable. Immediate-release (twice daily) and prolonged-release (once daily) tacrolimus are not interchangeable mg for mg; do not switch without specialist conversion and trough monitoring (label 2.1, 5.3). Doses shown are for immediate-release capsules. Topical ointment: no kidney dose adjustment.
kidney_function_basis: Not applicable for dose: tacrolimus is dosed by whole-blood trough concentration, not kidney function.

bands.recommendation: Dose by indication and whole-blood trough level (e.g., kidney transplant with mycophenolate and IL-2 receptor antagonist: 0.1 mg/kg/day in 2 doses, trough 4–11 ng/mL months 1–12) (label Table 1).

No kidney-function dose change: pharmacokinetics are similar in kidney impairment (label 8.6). Tacrolimus is nephrotoxic: dose by whole-blood trough levels; in liver, heart or lung transplant recipients with pre-existing kidney impairment use the lower end of the target range and reduce further if needed (label 2.4). Watch potassium.

hd.text: Not dialyzable; pharmacokinetics similar in dialysis patients (label 12.3). No supplement after dialysis; dose by trough levels.

pd.text: Not dialyzable (label); no PD-specific data. Dose by trough levels.

crrt.text: No data in label; not expected to be removed (high red-cell and protein binding). Dose by trough levels; specialist input.

dialyzable: No: not dialyzable to any significant extent (extensive red-cell and plasma protein binding; label 10).
monitoring: Immediate-release (twice daily) and prolonged-release (once daily) tacrolimus are not interchangeable mg for mg; do not switch without specialist conversion and trough monitoring (label 2.1, 5.3). Doses shown are for immediate-release capsules. Whole-blood trough levels; serum creatinine (nephrotoxicity), potassium, magnesium, glucose (new-onset diabetes), blood pressure, lipids; neurologic symptoms (PRES); ECG if QT risk; BK virus and CMV per transplant protocol.

pediatric.approved_ages: Liver, kidney, heart and lung transplant in pediatric patients (label 8.4).
pediatric.usual_dose: Kidney transplant: 0.3 mg/kg/day capsules or oral suspension in 2 doses, trough 5–20 ng/mL months 1–12 (label Table 1, pediatric).
